identity.title: TRACE: Your Diffusion Model is Secretly an Instance Edge Detector

problem.claim: Reduce the cost and scalability burden of obtaining high-quality instance and panoptic segmentation boundaries without dense instance-level annotations.

gap.claim: Existing unsupervised and weakly supervised methods remain limited by semantic-backbone constraints and human bias, often yielding merged or fragmented outputs.

contributions.claim: TRACE locates an Instance Emergence Point in diffusion self-attention maps, extracts boundaries with Attention Boundary Divergence, and distills them into a lightweight one-step edge decoder.
The design removes per-image diffusion inversion for faster boundary decoding.
TRACE uses diffusion-derived cues for unsupervised instance segmentation and tag-supervised panoptic segmentation without instance-level labels.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present text-to-image diffusion models as latent instance-edge annotators and propose decoding their boundary cues through TRACE.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report 81× faster inference, with sharper and more connected boundaries, after removing per-image diffusion inversion.
On COCO, the authors report a +5.1 AP improvement for unsupervised instance segmentation.
For tag-supervised panoptic segmentation, the authors report +1.7 PQ over point-supervised baselines without instance-level labels.

narrative_sequence.summary: Dense instance annotations are costly, inconsistent, and difficult to scale.
Unsupervised and weakly supervised alternatives can produce merged or fragmented predictions under backbone and bias constraints.
TRACE treats diffusion self-attention as a source of emerging instance boundaries, extracts them, and decodes them in one step.
The authors report substantially faster inference and gains on COCO instance and panoptic segmentation benchmarks without instance-level labels.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a specific internal signal—boundary emergence in self-attention—to a targeted decoder and reports both efficiency and task metrics.

lessons.interpretation: A compact paper narrative can align an interpretable intermediate cue with a concrete computational design and separately quantified outcomes.
lessons.application: When proposing a repurposing method, define the detected signal, the extraction rule, and the minimal downstream module before presenting task-level gains.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the intermediate signal cannot be operationally identified or independently measured.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify inference hardware, baseline configurations, absolute AP/PQ values, or statistical variability.
The conditions behind claims of sharper and more connected boundaries are not detailed.
The abstract does not establish whether the reported gains generalize beyond COCO or the stated supervision settings.
